name: Wood Grain
desc: The face of a sawn board running slowly past under a raking light — growth rings built from soft pale earlywood and a hard dark latewood band, dragged into whorls around the knots where branches left the trunk, and medullary ray fleck that flashes across the figure as the light moves.

rings.doc: growth rings across the board — tight rings read as slow-grown hardwood

scale.doc: how close the macro plate sits to the timber

energy.doc: chatoyance — strength of the raking sheen and the ray-fleck flash

density.doc: latewood width, surface tooth, and how many knots the board carries

cut.doc: where the saw took the board off the heart: 0 = through the pith (quartersawn — straight grain, ray fleck lights up) · 1 = well off it (flatsawn — the cathedral arches open)

hue.doc: re-tints the whole timber (26 = true warm oak/walnut)

speed.doc: how fast the board feeds past and the light crawls

y.doc: light elevation — sets where the figure lights up and how hard the fleck flashes

style.doc: oiled: finished hardwood, deep and warm, the figure alive under oil · bleached: limed/ashed pale timber, cool and dry · charred: shou sugi ban — the soft earlywood burnt out, embers still in the checks · xray: non-representational — a densitometry radiograph, latewood dense and bright, no material at all · ink: the plank as a woodblock print, grain pulled in sumi on paper

act.doc: plane: the board feeds steadily past under the cutter · season: the timber dries and moves across sections, rings tightening and easing · figure: a slow feed and a hard-working light — all chatoyance

seed.doc: a different tree — new pith wander, ring years and knot placement
